text:
AlertBot: paging: high p95 latency for /v1/generate — threshold breached (p95 > 800ms) on us-east-1, 3x sustained samples
Anya K.: ack, I'm taking this. grabbing initial context and tracing requests
Alex (on-call): i'm awake, jumping in with you @Anya K.  — what are customers seeing?
Anya K.: some proxy timeouts reported, 502s spike correlates with the latency window. affecting ~4% of requests over last 10m, mainly model-variant A on dedicated pool 2
Leo P.: putting a call into infra to see if there's a node OOM or network flake :phone:
Maria S.: saw increased queue depth on the serving-runtime logs, looks like KV cache misses spiking after last rollout
Samir R.: @Anya K. can you paste the alert query? i want to check if this is noise or true tail regression
Anya K.: alert def: ```
sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le) |> histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(...))) > 0.8
```
Samir R.: ok thanks. also seeing a small blip of tracer spans showing token-gen stalls on one host (i-0a12xx)
Alex (on-call): mitigation idea: route a fraction of traffic from variant A -> variant B (slightly higher cost but faster) and scale pool 2 by +2 GPUs temporarily
Leo P.: infra confirms one GPU on pool-2 reported driver resets around the time window. they're isolating the host now
DashBot: deploybot: canary rollback requested by @Anya K. — PR #4823 queued
Anya K.: rolling canary rollback of the variant in progress, switching 20% traffic now -> variant B as hot fallback
Maria S.: i'm enabling prefix KV caching on the serving runtime for the worst-offending route. doing a small config toggle now
Alex (on-call): monitoring error-rate and p99 latency dashboards — i'll post numbers in 2m
Anya K.: customer impact: initial spike caused increased latencies and transient 502s for ~4% of requests, no data loss, some customers reported slow UX. raising severity to sev-2 for now
Leo P.: host i-0a12xx has been cordoned. replacing and reprovisioning. looks like a GPU driver bug might be the root cause
Samir R.: after traffic shift + rollback, p95 dropped under 600ms and error-rate down to baseline in 4m — nice.
Anya K.: good. taking notes for post-incident: alert thresholds, dashboard gaps, encoding of fallback policies
Alex (on-call): handoff: Leo, can you take post-mortem checklist and own infra follow-up? I'll keep tracking the alert tuning and dashboards tomorrow. I'm heading offline in 20m
Leo P.: taking handoff. will open infra ticket and track host replacement.
Maria S.: filing a monitoring follow-up: current p95 alert is too noisy during rollouts. Proposal: change to p99 > 1200ms AND require sustained for 3 samples (5m avg) before paging.
Samir R.: also suggest adding a second alert: request_error_rate by route > 1% sustained 5m — fewer false positives and catches customer-facing regressions
Anya K.: agreed. We should also add a dashboard for incident retrospectives with drilldowns: golden signals for this service, per-variant breakdown, top traces, and node-level resource panels
Alex (on-call): here's a quick draft for the new Grafana dashboard panels (will open a PR):
- Panel: Request rate (per-route, per-variant)
- Panel: Error rate (5m, annotated with deploys)
- Panel: Latency histogram (p50/p95/p99) and heatmap
- Panel: Queue depth / prefix-cache hit rate
- Panel: Host health: GPU temp, driver resets, pod restarts
- Panel: Top 10 slow traces (link to Jaeger)
- Drilldown action: click on variant -> opens traces for that model variant and pod list
Maria S.: we should also add deploy annotations layer and an incidents panel that lists active/closed incidents with links to postmortems
Anya K.: agreed. priority items for follow-up (assign):
- infra ticket for host root cause + replacement — assigned to Leo P. — ticket INFRA-772
- Alert tuning: update p95 -> p99, add sustained window + new error-rate alert — assigned to Alex (on-call) — PR #4830
- Grafana dashboard: new incident-retro dashboard with panels above — assigned to Maria S. — dashboard draft at https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ijk987/incident-retro-draft
- Eval: model-variant stress test for KV cache behavior — assigned to Samir R. — test plan linked in the ticket
Samir R.: noted. i'll start the stress-run tomorrow and attach results to the ticket
Leo P.: INFRA-772 created. adding host logs and driver stack traces. ETA for replacement: 3h. :wrench:
DashBot: reminder scheduled: postmortem draft due in 48h — case: INC-2026
Alex (on-call): filing the alert change now. quick patch: ```
- alert: HighTailLatency
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le)) > 1.2
  for: 5m
  labels: {severity: page}
```
Maria S.: making the grafana panels — will add annotations for the rollback and the traffic shift times. also adding a panel to show "fallback routing applied" boolean for easy correlation
Anya K.: for retrospective, please ensure we capture: what happened, mitigation timeline, why alert fired, why rollout exposed this, and action owners. Also include quantitative customer impact: %requests affected, number of customers with degraded UX
Leo P.: adding postmortem skeleton to docs. assigning infra follow-up action items to myself and infra-oncall
Samir R.: found one flaky path in the KV marshalling which could amplify cache misses on edge cases. I'll PR a defensive fix after the stress tests.
Alex (on-call): p99 and error-rate remain stable at baseline now. I'm marking the incident as mitigated. will transition to postmortem workstream.
Anya K.: thanks everyone. quick retro note: moving forward let's route rollouts with canary QPS limits and add a pre-rollout heatmap check in grafana.
Maria S.: PR #4839 opened with dashboard JSON and panel mocks. Please review.
Leo P.: :thumbsup: closing my infra tasks for the handoff window. will follow up in INFRA-772
DashBot: incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring.
Anya K.: closing the thread here; action owners please update tickets and postmortem doc. next steps: review dashboard changes in PR, finalize alert tuning, run the stress tests. thanks all. :heart:
